LinPrim Optimization is the training procedure for Linear Primitives, using differentiable rendering to adjust primitive attributes (center, covariance, opacity, color) by backpropagating gradients from a composite L1 and SSIM loss through the entire rendering pipeline [S2].

The claim states that LinPrim Optimization uses differentiable rendering to adjust primitive attributes (center, covariance, opacity, color) via backpropagation of L1 and SSIM loss through the entire pipeline. Source [S2] explicitly confirms: 1) The use of differentiable rendering with L1 and SSIM loss terms from 3DGS; 2) Optimization using ADAM and backpropagation through the entire rendering pipeline; 3) The adjustment of primitive features including center, vertices (geometry), alpha (opacity), and color; and 4) The propagation of gradients through rasterization (affecting center/vertices/alpha/color) and preprocessing (affecting world space center, quaternions, and distances). While the claim mentions 'covariance' and the text mentions 'quaternion and distance features' (which define the shape/orientation, analogous to covariance in other Gaussian representations), the core mechanism and attributes described in the claim are fully supported by the provided evidence.
